skillLessons: Ear lower-pole gap cannot be fixed just by increasing sphere X scale: at the lower pole that radius tends to zero. Use explicit lower-lobe attachment and inspect both front and profile, plus outward ear orientation for side-chart readability.

Pure-profile eye width follows local face depth gradient; changing surface slope has the opposite effect of shrinking frontal eye width. Check front UV preservation and both oblique far-eye occlusions.
Broadening the bottom ring to round a frontal chin creates a flat cut. Use small bottom radius with nearby curved rings, then inspect front and both profiles.
Use rays/pixel RGB to classify neck gaps before shading adjustments. A complete upper jaw/neck joint can coexist with a separate low-neck/collar background hole.
